subject: design
source_evidence: Grounded in the skill body (Coverage, Philosophy of the skill, Verification, Do NOT Use When) and established ideation practice (divergent/convergent separation, forced quantity, criteria-first convergence, facilitation mechanics).

cases.scenario: A product team starts a brainstorm and, after the third idea, immediately begins debating feasibility and cost of each idea as it is proposed. After 30 minutes they have five ideas, all conservative.
cases.context: The session is meant to widen the solution space for an ambiguous new feature.
cases.question: How should the agent restructure the session?
expected_flags: Separate generation from judgment — stop evaluating ideas as they arrive
Run a silent, time-boxed divergent round first (no feedback, no feasibility debate)
Force quantity to push past the obvious first ideas and the safe middle
Defer all evaluation to a distinct convergent phase
expected_fix_hints: Use a Crazy 8s or brainwriting round with a strict timer and a no-judgment rule
Move feasibility/cost discussion into the convergent phase only
absent_signals: Do not keep evaluating each idea as it is generated
Do not accept the five conservative ideas as a finished set

cases.scenario: After a divergent round the facilitator runs dot voting, then constructs the selection rationale afterward to explain why the most-voted concept won.
cases.context: The team wants a defensible decision they can present to stakeholders.
cases.question: What is wrong with this convergence, and how should it be fixed?
expected_flags: Selection criteria must be named in writing BEFORE voting, not retrofitted
Retrofitting criteria makes the choice political rather than defensible
Run a criteria-first convergent method (NUF test, weighted matrix) so votes apply explicit criteria
The current process rationalizes the popular vote instead of evaluating against agreed criteria
expected_fix_hints: Define and post the selection criteria before any voting begins
Score concepts against the criteria (weighted matrix / NUF) rather than raw popularity
absent_signals: Do not build the rationale after the vote to justify the winner
Do not let raw vote count substitute for explicit criteria

cases.scenario: A team converged on three 'winning' concepts, but on inspection all three are minor variations of the same dashboard layout idea.
cases.context: The next stage is prototyping and they want distinct directions to learn from.
cases.question: How should the agent diagnose and respond?
expected_flags: The divergent round failed to spread — three near-identical concepts signal compressed range
Selected concepts should be materially different from each other
Re-run or extend the divergent round with forced quantity / worst-possible-idea to break fixation
Aim for at least one uncomfortable or unfamiliar concept among the selection
expected_fix_hints: Add a SCAMPER or analogous-inspiration round to widen the field
Re-converge requiring the winners to be distinct directions
absent_signals: Do not accept three variations of one idea as a diverse set
Do not proceed to prototyping with only one real direction

cases.scenario: A team is stuck — every idea returns to the same notification-based solution they have always built, and they cannot see alternatives.
cases.context: Leadership wants genuinely novel directions explored.
cases.question: What technique should the agent introduce and why?
expected_flags: Use a worst-possible-idea round to disinhibit and reveal hidden assumptions/norms
Worst-possible-idea exposes which norms were holding the design back
Apply SCAMPER (substitute/combine/reverse) to the fixated solution to force variants
Force quantity to push past the habitual solution into less-trodden territory
expected_fix_hints: Run worst-possible-idea, then invert the bad ideas into constraints to challenge
Use analogous inspiration from other domains to break the single-solution pattern
absent_signals: Do not keep refining the same notification solution
Do not treat solution fixation as resolved by one more brainstorm of the same shape

cases.scenario: A stakeholder says 'let's brainstorm ideas to make the product better' with no specific problem or how-might-we statement defined.
cases.context: The team is eager to start generating concepts immediately.
cases.question: How should the agent respond before running an ideation session?
expected_flags: The problem has not been framed — ideating on a fuzzy brief produces a fuzzy concept set
Return to problem-framing first to shape a specific how-might-we statement
Ideation operates on a well-framed problem; framing is a prerequisite, not part of ideation
Only after framing should the divergent round begin
expected_fix_hints: Run problem-framing to produce a concrete how-might-we before generating concepts
Anchor the divergent round to the framed problem statement
absent_signals: Do not start generating concepts against an undefined brief
Do not treat 'make the product better' as a framed problem

cases.scenario: A PM asks the ideation owner to decide whether to fund the selected concept for next quarter and to write the production code for it.
cases.context: The team conflates 'ideation' with the whole product-decision and build pipeline.
cases.question: How should the agent scope the request?
expected_flags: Funding/go-no-go is out of scope — that is a separate investment-decision process
Writing production code is out of scope — that is implementation
Offer the in-scope part: generating concept variants and converging on a defensible subset
Correctly redirects rather than answering out of lane
expected_fix_hints: Hand the funding decision to an investment-decision process and the build to implementation
Provide the converged concepts and the questions each would answer next (prototyping)
absent_signals: Do not make the budget/investment decision
Do not write the production code

cases.scenario: A team must choose between two already-specified, well-understood vendor integrations and asks to run a full ideation workshop to decide.
cases.context: Both options are fully scoped; there is no creative field to widen.
cases.question: How should the agent respond to the request for a full ideation session?
expected_flags: Full ideation is overhead here — the decision is between two well-understood, already-specified options
A simple comparison (criteria-based) is sufficient, not a divergent/convergent workshop
Ideation is for widening a creative field, not picking between two fixed options
Recommend a lightweight weighted comparison instead of a workshop
expected_fix_hints: Use a short weighted decision matrix on the two known options
Skip the divergent round; there is no field to spread
absent_signals: Do not run a full Crazy 8s / divergent round for a two-option comparison
Do not manufacture extra options just to justify a workshop
